title: protect.js: every workflow-run attempt link must carry ?pr=<number>, and both push sites must be kept in sync
answers: why does the Protect workflow-run link have a pr query parameter
how are attempt URLs built for Protect checks
my new Protect check link is missing the PR number
body:
Invariant: each check pushed by protect.js that links to a workflow run uses url = `${run.html_url}/attempts/${run.run_attempt}?pr=${pullRequest.number}`.
Enforcement: .github/workflows/protect.js:module.exports, in the two checks.push calls that build the url from run.html_url (the run-level status branch and the pending/failed branch).
What breaks: a link built without the ?pr= suffix differs from the others in the same log output. The two push sites duplicate the same URL template, so a change made to one site is not applied to the other unless both are edited.
applies: Any change to the URL format of checks in .github/workflows/protect.js, including new check sources that point at workflow runs.
says: The workflow attempt link in the protection check log is missing the pull request parameter.
Some test run links in the check summary lack the pull request query context.
Ensure all continuous integration run links in the protection log include the pull request.
Why do different check links in the status report format their run URLs inconsistently?
search: Workflow run URLs generated in .github/workflows/protect.js must include the attempt and the pull request number query parameter across both push sites. Applies to URL formatting in .github/workflows/protect.js:pullRequest where run.html_url, run.run_attempt, and pullRequest.number are formatted into checks.push. Modifying URL structure requires updating both the run-level status branch and pending/failed branch to prevent inconsistent link formats.
